note: Shows a step-choice as stages: one drill, three tempos, one chip each, so the metronome and the neck appear once instead of three times. The text names no tempo, says what a stage should feel like before the next one, where the chips are, that Play starts the metronome again, and what to do when a stage is too fast.

exercise.title: Position 1, faster in stages
exercise.focus: A minor pentatonic · position 1 · 60, 72, then 84 bpm
exercise.why: Your fingers learn the moves you repeat, clean or not, so each faster tempo comes only once the slower one is easy.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Play position 1 from the lowest {{1}} up to the high E string and back down, one note per beat.

When every note lands on the click without you rushing to reach it, tap Stage 2 above the metronome and press Play to start it again. If notes come late at a new stage, go back one stage and stay there a little longer.
